title.narrative: Readiness actions for potential new population movements in Oromia for integrated Emergency WASH, S/NFI, and MPC assistance (Fentale, East Wollega H/Guduru Wollega Zone)

description.narrative: ltpgtThis anticipatory action aims to strengthen preparedness and deliver timely, safe, and dignified humanitarian assistance to 60,922 people affected by both conflict and natural disasters, primarily focusing on newly displaced populations in the Oromia region. The intervention adopts an integrated approach with ZOA leading the delivery of Emergency Shelter/Non-Food Items (ES/NFI), Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH), and Multi-Purpose Cash (MPC) assistance.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe action is split into two phases depending on the crises happend and cluster recommendation:ltbrgt1. First Response: Aimed at IDPs from the Fentale Woreda in East Shewa Zone, following significant seismic activity and an earthquake in December 2024. This response begun in February 2025.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgt2. Second Response: Focused on East Wollega and Horo Guduru Wollega zones in Western Oromia, beginning in June 2025.ltbrgtContext: Fentale Earthquake Crisis (2024)lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtContext: Fentale Earthquake Crisis (2024): ltspangtFentale has been facing significant seismic activity since September 27, 2024, linked to the Fentale volcanic complex. On December 4, 2024, a 5.8 magnitude earthquake caused widespread damage, particularly in seven kebeles. Five of these were severely impacted, displacing 20,325 people (3,525 households). By early 2025, the number of internally displaced persons (IDPs) reached approximately 32,620 (5,500 households), with many now living in six IDP siteslt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe ongoing seismic activity, combined with a recent volcanic eruption, has destroyed homes, health centers, schools, roads, and livelihoods, severely disrupting daily life and transportation. While seismic activity has reduced recently, the situation remains unpredictable. These affected communities urgently need humanitarian assistance.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtConflict and Displacement in Western Oromia: ltspangtAccording to the 2025 Global Humanitarian Overview, conflict and climate shocks have caused widespread displacement across Ethiopia. Western Oromia, particularly Kellem Wollega, East and West Wollega, and Horo Guduru Wollega, has been heavily affected by ongoing violence since 2019, including insurgencies, cross-border attacks, and inter-ethnic conflict.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltspangtltbrgtlt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtSince 2021, clashes have spread to other Oromia zones, causing mass displacement and obstructing aid delivery, particularly along key routes like Addis Ababa–Nekemte–Assosa. Insecurity, poor infrastructure, and limited humanitarian access have left many communities without essential services such as healthcare, education, water, and shelter. Key challenges include:ltbrgt 426 health facilities are non-functional due to conflict and destruction.ltbrgt 144 schools in East Wollega remain closed, leaving over 62,000 children out of school.ltbrgt Criminal activities, including abductions and carjackings, are increasing, further endangering humanitarian workers.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtDisplaced Populations and Humanitarian NeedsltbrgtRecent assessments indicate:ltbrgt Horo Guduru Wollega: Jarte Jardega (3,707 IDP households) and Abe Dongoro (527 households) are the most heavily affected woredas.ltbrgt East Wollega: Haro Limu has 1,876 IDP households (7,504 individuals) in urgent need of WASH and emergency shelter.ltbrgtOverall, over 8,200 households (approximately 33,000 people) in priority areas are in urgent need of humanitarian support, particularly in Horo Guduru Wollega and East Wollega. Due to limited funding, ZOA plans to prioritize assistance for the most vulnerable populations in the Jarte Jardega, Abe Dongoro, and Haro Limu woredas following cluster recommendation.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltbrgt lt/pgt
